title: Seagate celebrates International STEM Day year-round
summary: Discover how Seagate employees inspire students through year-round STEM camps, classroom visits and hands-on engineering activities around the world.
body_markdown:
What does it take to inspire the next generation of innovators? Sometimes, it’s meeting an engineer, trying a new technology or discovering that getting the answer wrong is simply part of the process.


Celebrated each year on November 8, International STEM Day shines a spotlight on science, technology, engineering and mathematics and encourages young people to explore the possibilities these fields can unlock. The date itself carries a fitting message: “NOV8” sounds like “innovate,” reflecting the curiosity, experimentation and problem-solving at the heart of STEM.


At Seagate, that spirit comes to life through employees around the world who share their knowledge and experiences to help students see where their curiosity could take them. We support STEM education year-round in communities across the globe – take a look into


**Wuxi | STEM Camp**


Curiosity is often where innovation begins. At Seagate Wuxi’s FY27 Summer STEM Camp, 65 young learners ages 9 to 17 spent an afternoon exploring artificial intelligence, virtual reality, engineering challenges and other emerging technologies. Children of Seagate employees and students from the “Walking Classroom” community participated in hands-on activities designed to make science and technology approachable, engaging and fun, while encouraging them to ask questions, experiment and imagine where an interest in STEM might take them.


Powered by Seagate volunteers and teams across the Wuxi community, the event combined interactive learning with real-world perspectives from employees working in science, engineering and technology. From exploring how AI is evolving to hearing about STEM education and career journeys, students gained a closer look at the possibilities ahead. For Seagate employees, STEM Education Day was an opportunity to share their expertise and inspire the next generation of innovators, one question, experiment and discovery at a time.


**Derry/Londonderry | A future in STEM**


At Thornhill College in Northern Ireland, Seagate employees returned to the classroom to help the next generation of young women see where STEM could take them. During the Northern Ireland Space Showcase, students explored engineering through hands-on circuit-building activities and virtual reality demonstrations that offered a closer look at hard drive technology and nanoscale engineering. The experience was especially meaningful because Seagate engineers Lily Campbell and Amy English once attended Thornhill themselves, giving students real-world examples of how an interest in STEM can grow from the classroom into a technology career.


Together, Seagate and STEM Learning NI are developing additional opportunities to connect secondary school students with engineering, advanced manufacturing and the skills shaping the future of technology, helping young people not only learn about STEM, but see themselves as part of its future.


**Minnesota | STEM Outreach program**


In Minnesota, Seagate employees are helping K-12 students see themselves as the engineers and innovators of the future. Through Seagate’s Minnesota STEM Outreach program, volunteers bring STEM to life through classroom visits, workshops and community events. At a recent University of Minnesota Future Health Innovators Workshop, 43 high school students learned about hard drive technology and tackled hands-on engineering challenges that emphasized creativity, teamwork, problem-solving and learning through experimentation.


The program reflects a broader commitment to making STEM careers feel accessible and achievable by giving students opportunities to learn directly from Seagate engineers. From coaching students through the engineering design process to recognizing their achievements with Pioneer Awards created by Seagate’s Prototype Lab, employees are sharing both their expertise and enthusiasm for innovation. These experiences may last only a few hours, but they can help students build confidence, discover new possibilities and imagine a future for themselves in STEM.


Join Seagate colleagues around the world in sharing your knowledge, experience and passion for STEM with the next generation.[Learn more about how Seagate employees connect with each other and their communities.](https://www.seagate.com/careers/culture/)
